utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. First of all, my apologies for the delayed start. I was occupied by another business and couldn't be here in time. To discuss a confidential matter, we should briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I do not object to being in open session for stating this. I have some issues with the security. They only offer me some English tea which is causing me intestinal problems, and I'm forbidden to bring my own tea from the Detention Unit or any other tea brought to me by my counsel. For example, they used to bring me tea from the restaurant here at the Tribunal; however, I can no longer do that. I only eat once a day and if I don't drink a particular brand of tea, I have intestinal problems. I don't even eat the food that is provided in the Detention Unit. And without that particular tea, I wouldn't be able to take any further part in these proceedings. Could I please be allowed to drink the mint tea that I need, be it by bringing it from the Detention Unit, which I otherwise use there, or that my counsel be allowed to provide me with a cup of mint tea? Otherwise, I will have to refuse to keep drinking the type of tea, the only type of tea, I am offered by the security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. Perhaps I can be of assistance. Today, after over a year, we were told that I no longer can provide tea for Mr. Tolimir, for him to drink during the breaks in the course of the hearings. All tea that I used to bring him was purchased in the cafeteria here at the Tribunal. It is the mint tea I'm holding in my hand. And as of today I'm being forbidden to bring it to him, or actually I have to do that with the assistance of a guard. I don't know whose decision it was. The guard told me that he was instructed to do so by his supervisor. In any case, it is unreasonable, because we have been following the same practice as of day one of the proceedings, and all of a sudden, today, we can no longer continue with that. We are absolutely ignorant of any causes of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it that this is really a new development, a new occurrence, which didn't happen before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Mr. President. This is something we were told just prior to entering the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution have a position on that? Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Simply that whatever necessary inquiries are made to hopefully resolve the issue, and perhaps that can be done informally through the good offices of the Registry and the Trial Chamber and the members of the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, apologies. However, we have stopped receiving interpretation. Mr. Tolimir could not follow in the Serbian language what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should be checked first. Mr. Tolimir, do you receive translation -- interpretation of what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, I am now. But I received nothing when Mr. Thayer got up. There may have been a problem with his microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, would you please repeat your short comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. I was simply proposing that whatever the necessary inquiries are made and perhaps can be made informally through the good offices of the Registrar or the Trial Chamber and members of the Detention Unit or security that are present here, just to find out what the issue is. And hopefully it can be resolved that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, did you receive a proper interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I received the interpretation. All tests or examinations take a full month. Could we stop with the sessions for that one month, stop the hearings? During the tests I cannot take any food. When I started bringing in tea, all other accused started bringing in tea. And then when my proceedings started, I was prohibited from doing so. And then we made another arrangement which was that my counsel would bring it to me, and now that too is being forbidden. I don't know why that is such a problem all of a sudden. If the tea is a problem and if it needs to be tested or examined for months on end, then we should have stay in the proceedings. This here, the cafeteria of the Tribunal, is the last place that I can get that tea. I do not take food. For example, you can ask the guards that I have never taken a single meal in the Tribunal building. And I need that tea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the Chamber has considered your submission. I would like to ask, especially you, if you would agree that we make an oral decision now and ask the Registry to explain the situation, the reasons for the change of the proceedings in the Detention Unit, at the end of this session, before the first break, so that we are aware of the situation. Would that be sufficient for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please bear in mind that the DU puts entire meals in the van which also brings the accused and the drinks as well. But, however, I take none of that. I hand it all over to the guards. Perhaps another arrangement could be made that they no longer bring me the meal but only the tea?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I take it that you agree with our proposal to ask a representative of the Registry to explain the situation at the end of the first session of today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The application of the accused is on the record. The Registry is hereby ordered to explain the situation and the change in the proceeding in respect of providing tea for the accused at the end of the first part of today's hearing. That means in -- at 3.40 this afternoon in the courtroom. Thank you very much. If there's nothing else to raise before the witness is to be called in, then the witness should be brought into the courtroom, please. We go for a short moment into closed session to enable the witness to enter the courtroom. I just explain that for the public gallery. And then we go into closed session. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness received a caution in the last trial, and I think the circumstances still prevail.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Please stand for a moment. Good afternoon again, sir. Welcome to the Tribunal. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable. It's not the first time that are you giving evidence here in the Tribunal. You know the procedure, and you must be aware of the fact that that there are protective measures in place for you, so as using a pseudonym instead of your real name, and voice and face distortion so that nobody will recognise you outside of the courtroom. On the request of the Prosecution, I would like to caution you. We have one rule in our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This is Rule 19 -- sorry, 90(E) and I would like to read it out for you. I quote: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Sir, do you understand this rule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now Mr. Thayer for the Prosecution is examining you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you and Your Honours. Good afternoon to the Defence and everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 7251, and that should not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, in a moment you'll see a document on your computer. It is not being broadcast to the public. Without reading out loud anything that's on that document, I would just ask you whether you can confirm that you see your name written under the code-name PW-054. Just yes or no. Do you see your name there, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 7251, the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2052, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall testifying in this courtroom, in fact, for a little over two days in 2006?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you recently listen to that testimony?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you attest that the recording you listened to accurately reflected what you said during your testimony in that prior case?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Witness, you have a tendency to speak softly. If I could ask you just to move a little bit closer to the microphone, not too close but just a little bit closer, I think that might help. Now, can you attest that if you were asked the same questions today that you were asked back in 2006 that your answers would be the same?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter numbers 6679 and 6680, the transcript of the witness's prior testimony, the former being under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received, the former under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P2053 under seal and P2054 respectively, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, there are some associated exhibits, four to be exact. I can tender them now. Or if the Trial Chamber prefers, we can follow the other method of having Registry assign numbers separately. Whatever the Court prefers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken that there are -- these are only four, we can deal with that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well. The first associated exhibit is 65 ter 6681, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2055, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 65 ter 6682, also under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This will also be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2056, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The third is 65 ter 774.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This, too, will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2057.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And 65 ter 1630.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2058, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, as the Trial Chamber has probably noted, there are some associated exhibits which were used with the witness but not admitted in the prior proceeding, as well as two non-associated exhibits which were not part of the Prosecution's original 65 ter list of exhibits. Pursuant to our prior procedure, I've asked the Defence whether they have any objection to a Prosecution motion orally to move to add those two documents, that's 65 ter 7249 and 7250, to the Prosecution's exhibit list, and I'm told that there is no objection. I may not end up using these, but to be on the safe side I would orally move to add those to the 65 ter list at this time, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir or Mr. Gajic, are there any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, no objections. Only a piece of information that we would like to know. Are they already in e-court? The last time I checked, about two hours ago, they still have not been. It would be useful for us to know whether we can find it in e-court now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: They should already be uploaded, Mr. President, into e-court and available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And hopefully not only uploaded but released to the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And released, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Leave is granted to add them to the 65 ter exhibit list. Please continue, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have a 92 ter summary for this witness. And we had better go into private session for it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, we're back in open session. I'm going to show you some documents but we will not broadcast those documents. I'm going to ask you some specific questions about some of the passages in those documents but I will not refer to any particular names and would just ask that you not refer to anybody by name either. For example, I'll just refer to your unit, your commander, without referring to any names. And that way we can remain partially in public session but the actual documents will not be broadcast. Do you understand what I'm proposing?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All the other protective measures are still in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 7249. And this should not be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, we can see that what we have here is titled: "Record of a statement taken from a person." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And without saying what the date is or the location, can you tell the Trial Chamber, do you recognise what this is? And without identifying yourself, can you tell us the Trial Chamber whether you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Were you alone when this statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, there were maybe two other people present in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber whether or not on this same day, the date listed here on this document, other members of your unit were also asked to answer these same questions?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes. They also had to answer those questions. Only at different times.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Is it fair to say, then, that you and your fellow officers came in on the same day and just were interviewed at different times during the same day?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, obviously. That's what they told us to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there seems to be a technical problem. We can see very clearly the interpretation of what Mr. Thayer is saying, but we cannot hear the witness at all on channel number 6, B/C/S channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Registrar will try to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should continue and wait if the next response will be transferred to you in a sufficient way. Just pose, please, the next question to the witness, Mr. Thayer, and we will see how it works.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Now, if we could go to the next page of the document, please. And it will actually be the third page in both versions; forgive me. Next page. Great. And same thing with the original. Sorry, we'll have to go back one page in the B/C/S. I miscounted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we can see that with respect to virtually every question that was asked of you in this interview you responded, "I don't know"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The accused is receiving proper, yeah, or to call it transfer of the voice of the witness. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber just a little bit of an idea of what you and your fellow officers were told about this particular interview or set of interviews on this day?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, they told us that it was of a purely informative nature, simply to have some papers done, and for no other purpose than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, If we could go to the last page of the original, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, again, sir, this is not being broadcast outside this courtroom. Do you see your signature anywhere on this page?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just tell us on the page where is it located?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: On the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 7249.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2059, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And may we also have 6685 under -- without being broadcast, please. 65 ter 6685, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, again, sir, without identifying the exact date or location, do you see a document that's headed: "Record of a statement taken from a person"?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And seeing the date on this document and the location, do you recall providing a statement on this date and at this location?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I'm afraid we need to go into private session for the next question on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 6685, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2060, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may have 65 ter 6684 and not broadcast it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we can see here another document which is a record of a statement taken from a person. Without indicating the date or the location, do you recall giving a statement on this date, sir?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber whether the matters which you changed in this statement from your prior statement, whether those changes that you made in this statement were true or not? In other words, is this a true statement, this document that we have before us?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would tender 65 ter 6684, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to see the end of the text to know what it was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President. If we could go to the -- it would be page 4 in the English, where the actual statement begins. And if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What about the B/C/S version? It seems to be a very short one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. In the B/C/S version, the statement begins on page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, your last question to the witness was: "In other words, is this a true statement, this document we have before us?" And the answer was: "No." We should know which part was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Just some -- actually, to a significant extent he testified about this in the prior trial, but I will link the two up. And one of the reasons I'm actually going through the document is so that you can actually see the document, which we did not introduce in the last trial. But I will have to go back into private session to elicit specific detail about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told by the Court Officer that he is the relevant representative of the Registry to provide us with his knowledge and the necessary information about the application of Mr. Tolimir. Please inform us about the situation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. I have been authorised by the relevant sections of the Registry to represent the Registrar in making a submission regarding Mr. Tolimir's request to be provided that special tea during court hearings. I've been requested to inform the Trial Chamber that it is standard operating procedure adopted by both the UNDU and the security detail that Defence counsel and associates are not to provide anything to accused persons, especially food and drink. In this particular situation, security was -- the security detail today were not aware of Mr. Tolimir's special need for tea and hence were not providing it. For today, special arrangements have been made in this regard, and security will provide Mr. Tolimir with tea as a short-term immediate solution. So this will be implemented during the next break. Beyond today, and as a long-term solution, security has also been in association with the UNDU, exploring options to procure the required tea for Mr. Tolimir on an ongoing basis. In this regard, UNDU has offered to outsource the tea from its control stock, which they maintain generally to meet Mr. Tolimir's regular needs. So that should alleviate any concerns that Mr. Tolimir has in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Does that mean that the UNDU and the relevant staff will return to the proceedings previously in place?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: In this regard, Your Honours, the procedure envisaged is that the security personnel detail who are authorised to ensure the transport of Mr. Tolimir and ensure his custody in the holding cell will make available the required tea, and not the associates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not my question. My question is if the Registry is turning back to the previous procedure which was in place for more than one year.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: On the face of it, it does appear that the procedure will now be reversed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the Registry is not turning back to the previous procedure, it shall notify the Chamber as soon as possible. That means this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's duly noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The relevant information will be furnished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you have heard what the representative of the Registry told us. Please let us know how it will work today, during the breaks, and the next days, and if there is any concern, please let us know and update us about the situation. If there's a need to come back to this matter, we will do that. Thank you very much. We must have our first break now and resume quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I see Mr. Gajic on his feet. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be brief. I wanted to inform you of the latest developments concerning the tea provided to Mr. Tolimir. First of all, I need to mention that it is no special tea whatever. It's a simple mint tea. Secondly, Mr. Tolimir indeed received his tea, which is the same type of tea that we used to provide to him through the guards. I wanted to draw your fact to the following. Mr. Tolimir is not allowed to take any food or drinks, including tea, from the DU. I'd like to use this opportunity to thank you for your prompt reaction which resulted in this to everyone's satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Mr. Thayer, please continue your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And for my last couple of questions, we'll need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, now it's your turn for your cross-examination. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for everything have you done for the Defence today. I'd like to greet all those present. May peace reign in this house. And may today's hearing and the proceedings be concluded in keeping with God's will and not my own. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, given that we both speak the same language, you will have to follow the transcript in front of you; once the cursor has stopped, that means once it is recorded what we said, then we can start speaking again. Let us pause until such a time so as not to overlap. Let's start with page 39 of this transcript, or of this record. Mr. Thayer asked you why you were looking for the boy who was 16 then and would be 26 now, and he quoted page 6 in line 21 from the bottom. You said, Well, just so that I would know. Can you tell us, was he 16 then, as it is stated in the document, or was he older perhaps?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: He was 16 in 1995. Ten years later, of course, he was older.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Apologies to the interpreters. How do you know that? Do you know his date of birth? So that we could do our own maths and so that the Judges would know. Do you know what year he was born in?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know. But when I asked him how old he was, that is what he said. I don't see any reason for him to lie. That's what he said, although I don't know his exact date of birth. When I asked him how old he was, he said he was 16. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it mean that you took his word for it? Could he have been older at the time? Could you tell us that.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I took his word for it. And I could see him. I would have noticed had he been older.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know -- did you realize that Mr. Thayer stated his first and last name for the record and that they have information about him, also that he testified here and that we have his exact date of birth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask the witness to take off his earphones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sir, could you please take off your earphones for a moment. Is there a need to go into private session, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll try to keep it in open, Mr. President. We have a specific reference to a protected witness who testified before this Trial Chamber. That is a fact that we have to be very careful about protecting from the wider public. I placed the name in private session, but the fact that this witness has been told that a protected witness testified, we have to be very, very careful about, Mr. President, if we're gone to continue on this line. That very fact, I think, can obviously create a danger. But if we're going to continue with further questions, number one, they need to be in private session for sure, because of the protected nature of that other witness. I understand it's very difficult to examine this witness without any reference to that protected witness, but we have to be extremely careful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Protective measures mean not to give the identity to the public, including other witnesses. This is always the problem. Only the parties and the Chamber should know their real identity. If everybody, including Mr. Tolimir and the Defence, can bear that in mind, I think we should try to continue in that way as Mr. Thayer supposed. Would you agree, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I agree. I believe Mr. Thayer will agree, too, that both the Defence and the Chamber need to know exactly how old the person was in 1995 and whether he was a minor, as is alleged here. The Prosecutor probably knows that, given that the person involved appeared as their witness. We don't need to go into private session for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, in the presence of this witness, you can, of course, ask the witness if he knows more about the age of this young man. But to put other information to him will not help you. That can be done in the absence of the witness, I think. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, the way obviously we proceeded with Defence counsel in the prior case was simply to refer to another witness in this case testified that, without identifying, obviously, who exactly that witness was. And that's the minimum that we should be able to do to protect the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. The Court Usher will be asked to tell the witness to take on the earphones again. Sir, sorry for this interruption. There was a need for a discussion among the parties. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on. We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I cannot ask this question in open session, and I don't think that we are trying to protect the identity of that witness from this witness. I really see no reason for Mr. Thayer to hide that, since those two men were together and they know each other. This witness knows the identity of the other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not the question, I think, Mr. Tolimir, because -- Sir, can you please again take off your microphones [sic] for a moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the issue in a nutshell is that this witness ought not to be told that that other witness in fact testified. They may have met in 1995, but the fact that that other witness came and testified before this Trial Chamber should not be revealed to this witness. Now, whether this witness has found out that information through some other means, I have no idea. But the whole purpose of the protective measures is to protect, as Mr. President you've already said, not only the public but other witnesses knowing that other witnesses have come, if they are protected. Just like we wouldn't reveal this witness's identity to another witness who might come and testify. We would not do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we heard from this witness that he doesn't know if this other witness is still alive, that he was looking for him. And it should not be revealed what happened in the meantime, in the last 15 years, to this other witness. It is not -- it can't be our purpose to give this information to this witness. We don't know the result, we don't know what will happen to the other witness, to this witness, if they would be identified to each other. Because giving a pseudonym as a protective measures means that other witnesses don't know that other -- that they gave evidence in the courtroom in this trial. Only the parties and participants and, of course, the Chamber knows that. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as long as the witness is not able to listen, I can tell the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can tell the Trial Chamber, as an officer of the court, that my understanding is that this witness knows that the other witness is alive. He -- he has been told that, because he has asked us that because he wanted to know. And we have told him, it's my understanding, that, indeed, that witness is alive. My understanding is we have never confirmed that he has actually been a witness in this case or any other case. But just so the Trial Chamber understands, my understanding is that this witness knows that that boy, that young man that came and testified, is alive and that he had wanted to meet him. But that's as far as it's gone. So I just wanted to fill in the Trial Chamber on that portion of the story so you have a fuller picture. And I can represent that to the Trial Chamber from my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is helpful information. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Court Usher is again asked to help the witness take on the earphones again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Please, please, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, two claims have been brought forward here: First that he doesn't know whether the witness is alive; that's the first claim. And the second claim is that he was a minor at the time. I think that the Prosecution should show the Trial Chamber the documents about this witness because he testified here. And then we could all see whether he was minor at the time or not. That's something that this witness cannot know by himself. I certainly do not intend to reveal anything, but I also don't want anything to be secret that does not need to be secret. I think that all this data should be revealed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think we are dealing with a very serious matter at the moment. First I would like to check if we are in public or in private session. We are in public session. I would suggest that the witness leaves the courtroom until we have this problem resolved. Sir, we must have a sort break to discuss some procedural matters in your absence. Please follow the Court Usher and leave the courtroom for a moment, and we will call you back after we have discussed this matter. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we may go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, our apologies for getting you out of the courtroom and then back to the courtroom, but these are the procedures which we have to follow. May I put a simple question to you. We were talking about a young man at the age of 16 in 1995, as you described him. In 2005 you indicated that you didn't know about his fate, if he was still alive or not. What is your knowledge today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you know if he is alive or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I heard, I know that he's alive. But I don't know ... you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who told you that he is alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was somebody from the international police who told me that this person was alive and well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "international police"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know, the foreign police that we have there. I mean, those who were there at the time. It was them who told me that he was alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where did that happen? Where did you meet these people from the international police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And when did that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly. When was it? I think it was when I was giving the statement. Approximately then. I gave the statement in December in - what was it? - 2004. It was around about then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have seen some written statements of you this afternoon, and the latest one was from 2nd December, 2005, taking -- taken by the Bosnia and Herzegovinian Office of the Prosecutor. Are you referring to this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I refer to this statement as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you mean that the Prosecutor of the BiH is international police? Is that the same or are they different bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about two different bodies. But they both relate to this business, and I heard it through them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, I don't think anything about this body as international police. Was it Interpol, what we know as Interpol? Was it a Bosnian or Serb body, a body from the Republika Srpska? Can you tell us from which institution these people came who told you about the fate of this young man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were foreigners. Foreign police. International police. I don't know on what basis they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was an interpreter present when you talked to them and gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you recall which language they used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably English; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible that these people came from the International Tribunal, from this institution, here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't believe so. I don't know. Maybe they were. But nobody introduced them to me. They just told that they were international police, EUPM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Judge Nyambe has an additional question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: How exactly did you come to start discussing the boy with this organisation, whether it's BiH or international police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was in Tuzla doing certain things, and that's when I went to talk to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: What certain things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Well, you just said that -- I asked you in what circumstances you came to be talking about this boy with the police, whether BiH or international police. And you told me that "I went in Tuzla doing certain things, and that's when I went to talk to them." So I wanted to know, if you say, what things were you talking about? Did they call you, did you just go there yourself? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I went there on my own. And I also wanted to ask about him because there was some indicia; some people told me he was alive, some people told me he wasn't. And to tell the truth, if he was alive, I would felt sorry if he wasn't alive any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I hope the questions of the Chamber helped you to have a foundation for your further cross-examination. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: While we're on this subject, if I can just say that in the witness's prior testimony, which has now been admitted into evidence, this topic is addressed directly, starting at transcript page 4145, going all the way to 4150. This specific series of events, and generally these issues are addressed there, as they are in the 2 December 2005 statement which we had on the screen as well. In the section I brought to his attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us clearly, were you a member of the military or a member of the police? Here, during the testimony, it wasn't quite clear.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: First, I was a member of the military, until August 1994. After that, I was transferred; I went to work for the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, were you the active or the reserve force of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I was the reserve force. But I was attached to the active force, which means that I performed all the duties that the active force was performing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I apologise for not asking you precisely in my first question. When we are talking about the events in 1995, when you were in the so-called action to stop the Muslim column which moved out of Srebrenica towards the territory of your defence, were you then in the reserve or in the active force, and where exactly were you then?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I was in the reserve force, and I was somewhere around Snagovo. You know, when you go up from Zvornik past the hospital, it was about two or three kilometres from Zvornik. We didn't go any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you in Bijeljina before you were sent to Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just if we're going to start talking more specifically about particular locations, I just want to suggest that we may need to go into private session before we cross the line. I don't know where General Tolimir is going, but I just want to put everybody on the alert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, before you were sent to this particular assignment, were you in your police unit at the place where you were working at the time, or were you in the place where you performed this assignment?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I was in my own place before I went to perform this assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, were you accompanied by your commander, whose name is mentioned in your statement, when you went to perform this assignment?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. He didn't go with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So was he, your commander, able to issue orders to you in the field if he wasn't with you, present, when you went to perform that task?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell me, when you went to perform this assignment there, did you get another commander who commanded you during the performance -- while performing this assignment?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, there was this guy who used to be a commander, the brigade commander. He went with us there. But he didn't give us any specific order. Or maybe he did, but I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, did you work in accordance to the order issued by your commander from your place, your police station, or according to the orders of this person to whom you were attached and to who then issued the order? Maybe you were subordinated to something.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, our commander issued us an order. Nothing specific was ordered to us there at the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is, actually: Did you get specific assignments what you were supposed to from the commander of your police station, or were you supposed to get such instructions from the one to who you were resubordinated for the performing of that assignment?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, we just need a redaction at page 57, line 3. It might be line 5 on -- on the Trial Chamber's screen. But there's a specific reference to a location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, that will be redacted. Mr. Tolimir, please put your question you were going to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I don't know what my mistake was because -- but I don't need to know either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It was not your mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber whether there were only police officers from your station to perform that assignment or were there others from other police stations?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: There were police officers from other police stations too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, how did they go about it then? Did everybody have the orders issued by their commanders, original commanders, or by the commander to who they were resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Probably they got their instructions from the commander when they set out, or maybe they got them when they arrived at the site. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I warned you, this is a court of law, and if you tell me that the relevant thing was what was told to us when we arrived at the army, or that the relevant thing was when we started throwing the grenade, so please give me a clear answer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer, otherwise we really can't interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, frankly I'm not sure what's going on. But what I read is the accused warning the witness that this is a court of law and then making a reference to throwing a grenade, and I'm not sure what the basis is anywhere for either of those statements. I don't think it's the accused's role to warn this witness about the fact that this is a court of law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't understand that either. The whole question is -- was unclear, in my view. And there I don't find any real question. But, again, the request of the interpreters is to pause between question and answer. And I would like to invite the witness to speak up a bit to the microphone. Sometimes your voice is very low, and it's very hard to hear you. Mr. Tolimir, please continue. And put a question to the witness which we can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please tell us, would every police officer who had come from different police stations in the RS have to do what he was told by the commander to whom he was subordinated in combat or what he was told by the chief of the station who sent him to that joint force?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, he would have to do what he was told in the field. That's what he should do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that you carried out the orders of those commanders who commanded you daily in the field; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did the chiefs of the SJBs in your towns, because you were from various towns, tell you what you were supposed to do in principle?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: They gave us wrong information. They said that we were to mop up the territory, that there would be people from the different stations, and that there would be someone from the centre who -- to be in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just used the term "mopping up." Can you tell us, were you sent out on the assignment to prevent the passage of the convoy from Srebrenica from coming -- from coming behind our backs or mopping up the terrain?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: As far as I understood, it was to mop up the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you prevent the enemy from piercing the front line and coming up behind our backs? I mean the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have a big problem with this kind of conversation. The interpreters didn't catch because both speakers start immediately after having heard the other speaker. You both have to pause. It is very difficult for the interpreters. The -- there was -- the last question for the witness: "Did you prevent the enemy from piercing the front line and coming up behind our backs? I mean the Zvornik Brigade." That was the question of Mr. Tolimir. Could you answer this question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had no contact with the military whatsoever there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The units from the police stations that made up one unit, did these police officers have the assignment to protect the town of Zvornik from those who were coming from the direction of Srebrenica or did they have another assignment?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you get instructions as to what you were supposed to protect, the back of the unit that was defending itself toward Nezluk or the citizens in the places where they lived? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We couldn't protect anybody's back because we were in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. And did the enemy cross that line that you guarded?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes. They were -- there was some forest. I don't know where they belonged. But that was my first time out there, so I didn't know my way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And if the enemy were to pierce the lines that you secured, could they encounter our army that defended itself toward Nezluk and attacked them from the back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please, please wait --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, probably they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please wait and pause. Not immediately give an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please tell us, did you hear or take part or see that part of the convoy that you were to prevent from passing through passed through anyway toward the units that defended itself against the enemy who was coming from the direction of Nezluk?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No, I heard nothing of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you go about your assignment conscientiously, and did you prevent the enemy from attacking our units from the back?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I think we did. We would certainly have held our section no matter what.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Apologise to the interpreters. Did your commander at the place where -- from which you were deployed to your combat operation order you that not even a fly may be allowed to pass through because he wanted to prevent the situation where the enemy could come behind our back of our units that were defending themselves? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that you had to perform your task conscientiously so that those whose backs you protected do not come to harm?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us take a look at page 3 now. 65 ter 06683, the Prosecution's 65 ter list. Page 3. Line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is now P2063, under seal. It should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In English it's page 4 of document P2063. Line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see your answer here, where you say: "That not even a fly must be allowed to -- to come out from there." That was ordered by your commander, and I don't want to read out his name.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was it that way?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If you remember, in your statement, and you were asked also by the Prosecutor about this, you understood this to mean that you had to kill everybody. Couldn't it have meant that you were to prevent anybody from passing through, rather than killing everybody? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, prevent too. But you know how it is in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If that meant that you were meant to prevent enemy soldiers to cross the line that you held, does it mean that you had to kill everybody or keep them from -- from -- or prevent them from crossing the line? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer. It was a kind of prevention. If they had shot at us, then we would have shot back. They were in front of us, the small group. And about the rest of them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll talk about the small group later. Could we please show D155 to the witness from e-court to see what those who passed by the line you are meant to guard did. And it came up behind the back of the forces that were on the front line. Thank you. I'm talking about a document dated 16 July 1995. We can see it here. It's a report on the situation in Srebrenica. It was sent through the security department. Let us see pages 2 and 3. You will see to who it was sent. It was sent to Alija Izetbegovic, but it's not really legible here. And here it says -- down there you see the heading, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, General Staff of the army. So it's the Army of BH who -- that sent it on 16 July.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please go to the following page. They are sending it to President Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And take a look at the last paragraph, paragraph 3. We can see it in Serbian. It's page 3 in English. We can see what it says: "The units of the 28th Division of the KoV are pulling out of Srebrenica while still fighting. The units of the 28th Division of Kov have remained compact. In the temporarily occupied territory they have scored success after success. They are inflicting heavy losses on the aggressor. They have eight Chetniks (alive) in captivity. Units of the 28th Division of Kov have linked up with the infiltrated units of the 2nd Corps. The joint forces have continued fighting in the temporarily occupied territory. It is expected that they will fully link up with these units soon. Activities are under way to exploit the success of the units making the breakthrough." Now my question is the following: Did you hear later, if not then, that there was a breakthrough and that there were even prisoners, as Mr. Delic says here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. We didn't know about this document at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that you didn't. But did you hear that there was fighting and that this unit was fighting its way out of Srebrenica to the Muslim-controlled territory at Nezluk? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anything about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you know whether our forces had losses or soldiers taken prisoner and injured soldiers on that line of which the commander said that not even a fly can be allowed to pass through?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No, we didn't know a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We'll see another document now, which is D176.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please display it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: While we're waiting, this is another document by the Muslim army, so you don't get the impression we're talking -- we're giving our own story. It is dated 27 July 1995, immediately after these events, and it's entitled, "Chronology of Events." And we see that it was sent to the attention of Commander General Rasim Delic. It says: "Enclosed please find the complete chronology of events from the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you are quoting from this text, I see Mr. Thayer on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just wondering if there is a list of cross-examination documents. We -- we haven't received one. I understand sometimes these things happen, but we haven't gotten a list. I don't know how long the list is. If it's just these two documents, okay, we can deal with that. But if there's going to be more, we'd like to have a list, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Chamber has received such a list. I don't have one with me. Mr. Tolimir, can you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this document was not forwarded to the Prosecution. However, given that the Prosecution tried to show this combat activity as a mop-up operation rather than stopping the enemy, I had to show these documents to illustrate that these front line activities were of a different nature. It was not a mop-up operation. By your leave I would like to use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Tolimir, this is -- was not the problem which Mr. Thayer raised. The problem is a different one. I think we didn't receive, as we normally get, a list of documents to be used during your cross-examination. This is a normal requirement. Did the Defence send a list or not? Perhaps Mr. Gajic can help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it was our original intention to only rely on the documents which are otherwise on the OTP list which they intended to use with the witness. However, during the examination, some issues came up. That is why Mr. Tolimir is now relying on another document which was not on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: On the list of the Prosecution, you mean. We would appreciate if we can get an information now how many and which documents you are going to use to enable the Prosecution to prepare the -- the re-examination. This is the normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the last one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's fine --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This will be the last document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's fine. Just go ahead, Mr. Tolimir. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to you and the OTP, given that we didn't notify them of these documents. That is why I chose to show these documents in a collective fashion so as not to have to go one by one. This document was sent by the commander of the 2nd Corps. Could we please go to the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You can see the chronology of events of the 3rd of June. You can see the dates. We see that it ends with the 8th of July on this page. Now we can move on to the next so that you can see all the things that took place at the time. As a plain soldier, of course, you were not as familiar with the situation as the commanders were. Now we can see the 9th of July, the 10th of July, the 11th.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please, to see the date to which witness is actually testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see the 13th and the 14th of July. You mentioned the 14th of July here. Is that correct? Did it all take place on the 14th or the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date anymore. But the 14th or the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what the situation was at the front lines on the 14th of July. I quote: "The 24th Land Forces Division" -- and here we have strictly confidential number. It is actually the Muslim 24th Division. I apologise I missed something. "On 14 July 1995, the 2nd Corps command sent to the commands of the 21st, 22nd, and 24th Division of the Land Forces orders," strictly confidential number as stipulated, "to prepare and send volunteer companies to conduct offensive combat operations in the area of responsibility of the 24th Division of the Land Forces with the aim of providing assistance and co-ordinate action in the combat actions of the 28th Division of the Land Forces, which is moving in a breakthrough towards the area of responsibility of the 24th Division. On the same day, the 2nd Corps commander issued a task to the 24th Division commander to deploy and plan a co-ordinated action with the units of the 28th Division that had set out to break through."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We saw what happened on the 24th. Since you were not certain of the date, look at the 12th line. It says the 15th of July. I quote: "In the morning on the 15th of July, 1995, in the general area of Snagovo and Glumina, significant combat took place and we learned from counter-electronic warfare units that some 28th Division units were engaged in combat with the aggressor. At the same time, in the area of responsibility of the 24th Division, following the order of the 2nd Corps commander," we see what the number of the order was, "all units of the 242nd Motorised Brigade returned, as well as the 24th Crni Vukovi unit, which until then had been deployed in the area of responsibility of the 110th Light Brigade. And in the afternoon, on the 15th of July, units of the 21st, 22nd, and 25th Division, a total of 876 [as interpreted] troops, were relocated to the area of responsibility of the 24th Division at the 2nd Corps, orders strictly confidential," we see the numbers, "so that the 24th Division command, together with its free forces, had 1.430 troops at its disposal. "From 1200 hours on the 15th of July," et cetera, "from the firing position of Meskovici, Zvornik was fired on," meaning that it -- the fire came from the territory controlled by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We see the order numbers. We now move on to the 16th, but let me ask you this first. Were you in any of the location referred to in these Muslim reports about the activities of their units towards Zvornik, as well as the activities of their artillery supporting those breaking through to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, that was a very long question. In fact, a long quote and a very short answer. But we must have our second break now and resume in half an hour. Before we do that, Mr. Thayer has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we've -- we have a witness who's been on stand by. Just wondering whether we can release that witness. I don't know what the Defence's remaining cross estimate is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimation, Mr. Tolimir? Have you any idea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If Mr. Thayer will have no re-examination, I will be finished with this witness today. There are still some key questions that I need to put to this witness, given the fact that he changed some of his statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In that case, the next witness should be released, Mr. Thayer. We adjourn and resume quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Sir, we have now seen that almost three divisions of the BH army were attacking our forces from the front line in the Baljkovci [as interpreted] region in front of Snagovo where you were and one division was attacking from the back, the 28th, which was making breakthrough from Srebrenica. Here's my question: Did the VRS which was preventing the division from Srebrenica from passing through by its activity contribute to alleviate the pressure on the forces on the front line toward Nezluk?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And was it your task to prevent the 28th Division from passing through so it doesn't reach enemy territory? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: But what did you know? What did you know to be your task?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Nobody put it to us the way you -- you just have. We -- they just sent us there and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were not familiar with your exact task when you were out there in the field?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the chiefs of the police stations of your original units to who the request was sent happen to know which area you were to seal off and prevent the enemy from passing through? Did they know?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, probably they did, but we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did your commander know, when he said that not even a fly may be allowed to pass through, did he know that you were defending the back of the unit that was defending itself from the three divisions that we saw mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, probably, but we didn't know. He may have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your commander a conscientious commander when it comes to carrying out tasks? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, in some things he was conscientious, I think. And that the two of us didn't get along very well was another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for this honest answer. Tell us now, the soldier whom you brought to your police station from the front line, did your commander demand that you kill him or that you take him to the POW centre?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We took him to our station and it was up to him to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When he decided that he should be sent to Batkovici, as you say in your statement, was that his decision or yours?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, I was subordinate. He was my boss.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Superior not subordinate. Could the accused please repeat his question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please repeat your question. I think you were overlapping again and there were many mistakes in the transcript, if I'm not mistaken. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 71, in line 13, it says "Bosnia." Yes, I was -- oh, I see now it's been corrected. Yes, he was my boss. Now it's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I would like to mention that in line 5 of the current page there's the beginning of the question of Mr. Tolimir. I would like to remind both speakers again to pause between questioning and answering. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will repeat the question that overlapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did your commander act correctly when he sent the prisoner to the POW centre or camp at Batkovic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was this prisoner later registered and exchanged, as far as you know? Do you know whether he was exchanged later and whether he left to BH army-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But a minute ago you said that you learned from the international police that he was alive and well, or, rather a short time ago. Does that mean that he was exchanged? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes. It was a considerable time later though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you visit the prisoner while he was at Batkovic camp? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you, Mr. Tolimir. You -- Sir, you were asked by Mr. Tolimir: Do you know whether he was exchanged later? And now I see you answered this question. Thank you very much. Go ahead, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please tell us now about your statement which was quoted by the Prosecutor and which was amended several times and changed. Did you give that statement based on your assumptions of the actions of the commander or based on precise orders received?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Because, as we all know, there are a number of statements we're talking about, it might be helpful if General Tolimir specifies which statement he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I certainly can. I had in mind the statements in Bijeljina and in the Muslim part of Sarajevo, as well as the statement in Tuzla. Those three statements. All signed by the witness. I don't have enough time to discuss it at length as to why it was done in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm just asking the witness whether he provided those statements based on his presumptions or based on clear orders that were issued?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, they were based on what I thought about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone in Sarajevo or Tuzla promise you anything, any kind of compromise or an arrangement to be made, so that you would provide such statements?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. No one did any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it for that reason that you went to Sarajevo and Tuzla, in order to provide the statements, and did it all have to do with the issue of the workplace you were promised and your livelihood?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, yes, all that and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us whether you saw for yourself anyone committing illegal acts such as killing enemy soldiers? Can you mention anyone by name?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No, I cannot. I don't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
