utterances.text: Thank you. Were all the statements and assertions made therein about the alleged victims given based on your presumptions and rumours you heard, or were they based on what you could see yourself?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Only based on what I could see. There is some hearsay, but I don't take anything for granted, unless I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I just asked whether you saw anyone killing anyone else.

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I don't know who that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did it take place as part of the combat your unit was engaged in or was it in non-combat circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: The place I was, was out of combat. There was no combat at that time where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you performing a task, since you say that it was a non-combat situation?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes. We were on an assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was it around the clock that you were performing that assignment or only in day-time?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: In the course of the day. In day-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it necessary because of that to again search the terrain to make sure that there were no enemy forces left over?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. We were just there during the day. And in the evening we would go back to our initial positions for two or three days. And then we went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did it always involve a single location at the front line or did you move about?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We were only at that one location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If you were performing all of your tasks at a single location, could you have, indeed, participated in a mop-up operation, as you stated, in order to prevent the enemy from breaking through?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We were in that one location. We didn't go any further afield.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you assigned tasks on the spot by the commander so as not to allow any armed forces of the 28th Division to break through your positions?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: We received such tasks. But, luckily enough, they didn't come our way. I don't know in what direction they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Save for promises, were you offered any benefits or positions in order to change your statements this way or that way?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we conclude that no one had anything to win in that situation or that there was nothing that -- no gain for you in the changing of those statements?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: No. Neither myself nor anyone else could benefit from those changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the fact that you changed statements a number of times carry with it a possibility of creating consequences for those involved in your statements?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, one could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could we say, then, that no one suffered any consequences based on what you stated?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir please repeat the last question. It was a compound question which was not understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters asked you to repeat the last question because they didn't catch the content of it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How should we put this, Aleksander? Thank you. I asked whether anyone suffered any consequences because the statements were changed, be it before a national court or before this Tribunal, and the witness answered no, if I recall that correctly. Perhaps he can provide his answer again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did anyone suffer any consequences before national courts in Bosnia or in the RS or before the International Tribunal because of that?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you content to find out that the person whom you saved in wartime remained alive?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite happy because of that. And I believe I've been quite realistic in all this. I mean no harm to anyone. Such was the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: When we sum it all up, is it better that all this was concluded without any consequences for you or anyone else, irrespective of the fact that you were not provided the job you had been offered or had not obtained any material gain?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for having come here and testified. I won't put any further questions so as to allow some time for the Prosecutor to examine you, if necessary. Thank you for everything you said, and thank you for not causing harm to anyone. Thank you again. May God bless you. Have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence have no further questions of this witness, and we don't want to keep the witness until tomorrow because he has been waiting to testify for a while.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tolimir. I have only one single question for the question at the moment. On page 72, lines 16 and 17, you were asked by Mr. Tolimir: "Does that mean that he" - and he was referring to this young man - "was exchanged?" And then you answered: "Yes. It was a considerable time later though." How do you know that he was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found out that he is alive.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his last sentence. It was inaudible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you move a little bit further to the microphone, please, and speak up a bit and repeat the last part of your answer because the interpreters didn't catch it. You answered my question. "I found out that he is alive." How did you find out that he was exchanged? Or is it an assumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were rumours, assumptions, and such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Carrying on, on the issue of the young man you moved from the area back to your police post, who did you hand him over when you get -- when you got there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We handed him over in the station, in our police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Do you know to whom in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had our commander. There was no one else to hand him over to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Is this the same commander who gave you the instructions when you were going out to the field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just follow up on that last question from Honourable Judge Nyambe. When you returned to your police station with the boy and, as you just said, handed him over to your commander, did you do that alone, or did you do that with someone else?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Together with the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "the rest," to whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: I have in mind the people I went with, our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And had there been any decision of any kind beforehand to bring the boy in as a group, or was that something that just happened by accident when you returned to the station?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: By -- by chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you brought this boy to your commander, can you tell the Trial Chamber - and please don't feel shy about repeating as much as you can remember of your commander's exact words; we're all grown-ups here - so what did your commander say to you when, as you said before, he got angry and attacked you for bringing back the boy alive? What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: You mean when we arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. When you arrived and you handed the boy over to him, when he saw that you had brought this boy back alive, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: He was very upset with us for having done that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last sentence. He was inaudible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind you to speak up a bit and to speak into the microphone. The interpreters didn't hear you. Please repeat the last part of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was very upset with us for having done that. He said, What do you think Bando [as interpreted] will have to say about that? It was a man who had some sort of a paramilitary unit of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did he make any reference to the order he had given you?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what your commander said to you when you brought that boy back alive regarding the order he had given you?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Why did you do that? Why did you bring him? You knew what the orders were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, just picking up on something that General Tolimir asked you about, he asked you about your commander, and you told the Court that despite the personal differences, the disagreement, that you had with your commander, you considered him to be conscientious. Do you remember that question and answer from a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a couple of questions. This commander that we've been talking about, in your experience working for him as a subordinate, was he a commander who followed orders that he was given, or was he a commander who did not follow orders he was given?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, I think he followed the orders in keeping with his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in your experience working for your commander, did you ever know him to fail to carry out any order he was given?

utterances.speaker: PW-054
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, he didn't. But I didn't really move in those circles. I wouldn't real know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could go into private session, just for my last question, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, this concludes your examination here in The Hague, in the Tribunal, in this case. The Chamber would like to thank you for your attendance here, that you came to The Hague and provided us with your knowledge. Now you are free to return to your home and to your normal activities. Thank you very much. We should go into private --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thanks to everybody.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have to adjourn and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
